items.title: Warren Bernhardt interviewed by Monk Rowe, Bearsville, New York, January 3, 2012
items.q: I stumbled in Debussy’s “Fireworks” ... and I improvised about a four bar section there that Debussy never thought of

ctx.x: If you were in the middle of a classical piece and you stumbled, could you improvise your way out of it and back into it?

Yeah, yeah. It feels pretty bad. It’s awkward. I did it — that same concert that — I recorded the concerts a couple of years ago here in Woodstock and I stumbled in Debussy’s “Fireworks” — it’s Feux d’artifice — and I improvised about a four bar section there that Debussy never thought of, but I managed to get it and come back. And listening back to the tape it’s like, oh no, oh, oh, okay, you got it back. I mean I came from a different age, and all these conservatories are turning out these technically perfect —…
You were under the piano when Rubenstein was playing?
